cards.front: What did Java 17 make permanent?
cards.back: Sealed classes and interfaces, and pattern matching for switch (preview then) — plus it is the LTS after 11
cards.extra: Sealed types make exhaustive switch checking possible, which is the feature's real payoff.
cards.merge_into: 00 Java Roadmap::03 Language Features::00 Overview

cards.front: What does a pattern switch add over instanceof chains?
cards.back: Arms with type patterns and guards (case String s when s.length() > 5), checked for exhaustiveness
cards.extra: The compiler verifies that every permitted subtype is covered — the reason sealed hierarchies pair with it.
cards.merge_into: 00 Java Roadmap::01 Foundations::04 Conditionals

cards.front: What did Java 16 finalise?
cards.back: Records, pattern matching for instanceof, sealed classes (second preview), and Stream.toList()
cards.extra: It is the release where records stopped being a preview and became usable in production.
cards.merge_into: 00 Java Roadmap::02 Object Model::18 Record

cards.front: What did Java 15 deliver?
cards.back: Text blocks (final), hidden classes, and the sealed-classes preview
cards.extra: Text blocks ended the triple-escape era for SQL and JSON literals.
cards.merge_into: 00 Java Roadmap::03 Language Features::00 Overview

cards.front: What did Java 14 add that changes everyday debugging?
cards.back: Helpful NullPointerExceptions, switch expressions (final), records (preview) and jpackage
cards.extra: The NPE message names the exact expression that was null — the single largest quality-of-life change in years.
cards.merge_into: 00 Java Roadmap::13 JVM and Tooling::01 JVM Internals

cards.front: What did Java 13 bring?
cards.back: Text blocks and switch expressions as second previews — no permanent language changes
cards.extra: Java 13 and 14 are where these features were refined before standardisation.
cards.merge_into: 00 Java Roadmap::03 Language Features::00 Overview
cards.example:
String text = """
    hi
    """;                                     // text block: preview in Java 13
int n = switch (1) { case 1 -> 10; default -> 0; }; // switch expression: second preview in 13
System.out.println(text + n);                // neither was permanent in 13

cards.front: What did Java 12 introduce?
cards.back: The switch expression preview, Collectors.teeing, CompactNumberFormat and Files.mismatch
cards.extra: Most of the API additions survive; the switch change needed two more releases.
cards.merge_into: 00 Java Roadmap::03 Language Features::00 Overview

cards.front: What was Java 10's headline feature?
cards.back: Local variable type inference — var
cards.extra: It is the only language change in 10; everything else was GC and runtime work.
cards.merge_into: 00 Java Roadmap::01 Foundations::03 Data Types

cards.front: Why do static analysers ask you to hide the implicit constructor?
cards.back: A utility class with no explicit constructor can be instantiated and subclassed by mistake
cards.extra: A private no-arg constructor makes the intent explicit and blocks both.
cards.merge_into: 00 Java Roadmap::02 Object Model::04 Static Keyword

cards.front: When would you use a default method instead of an abstract class?
cards.back: When implementors already extend something else — an interface still lets them take the method
cards.extra: Default methods give behaviour without consuming the single superclass slot.
cards.merge_into: 00 Java Roadmap::02 Object Model::16 Interfaces

cards.front: Are static interface methods inherited?
cards.back: No — they are not inherited by implementing classes or subinterfaces
cards.extra: You must call them through the interface name: MyInterface.helper().
cards.merge_into: 00 Java Roadmap::02 Object Model::16 Interfaces

cards.front: How are interfaces declared inside a class or interface treated?
cards.back: They are implicitly public static
cards.extra: Nesting is purely for namespacing — there is no outer-instance relationship.
cards.merge_into: 00 Java Roadmap::02 Object Model::16 Interfaces

cards.front: What does the diamond operator infer?
cards.back: The type arguments of the constructor from the assignment target: List<String> l = new ArrayList<>();
cards.extra: With anonymous classes it required Java 9 — before that the diamond was illegal there.
cards.merge_into: 00 Java Roadmap::04 Collections::09 Generics

cards.front: What makes a class a POJO?
cards.back: Only that it is an ordinary Java object — no framework interfaces, no required superclass
cards.extra: It does not even require getters or a no-arg constructor; that is JavaBeans, a stricter idea.
cards.merge_into: 00 Java Roadmap::02 Object Model::01 Classes and Objects

cards.front: What are the rules for an immutable class?
cards.back: Final class, all fields private final, no setters, defensive copies of mutable inputs and outputs
cards.extra: Records give shallow immutability only: a mutable component still lets state change.
cards.merge_into: 00 Java Roadmap::02 Object Model::01 Classes and Objects

cards.front: Does Java support default parameter values?
cards.back: No — the idiom is overloads delegating to one full method
cards.extra: The alternative is a builder or a parameter object when the count grows.
cards.merge_into: 00 Java Roadmap::02 Object Model::02 Attributes and Methods

cards.front: What is the difference between !a and a != true?
cards.back: Both invert a boolean, but !a is the idiom; comparing to true is noise
cards.extra: For boxed Booleans !b unboxes and can throw NPE — Boolean.FALSE.equals(b) is null-safe.
cards.merge_into: 00 Java Roadmap::01 Foundations::04 Conditionals

cards.front: Why compile a regular expression once?
cards.back: Pattern.compile is expensive; a static final Pattern is reused across calls
cards.extra: Compiling inside a loop is one of the most common avoidable performance bugs.
cards.merge_into: 00 Java Roadmap::01 Foundations::09 Strings and Methods

cards.front: How do you count regex matches in a string?
cards.back: Loop on Matcher.find(), or use results().count() (Java 9+)
cards.extra: split() gives you the parts, not the matches, and differs on trailing empty strings.
cards.merge_into: 00 Java Roadmap::01 Foundations::09 Strings and Methods

cards.front: How do you compute a checksum in Java?
cards.back: CRC32 for speed, MessageDigest (SHA-256) for cryptographic integrity
cards.extra: A checksum detects accidental corruption; only a keyed digest or signature detects tampering.
cards.merge_into: 00 Java Roadmap::07 IO, Network, Data Formats::01 I-O Operations

cards.front: How do you generate an RSA key pair in Java?
cards.back: KeyPairGenerator.getInstance("RSA") with a key size, then generateKeyPair()
cards.extra: Then Cipher with RSA/ECB/OAEPWithSHA-256AndMGF1Padding — never the bare "RSA/ECB/PKCS1Padding" default.
cards.merge_into: 00 Java Roadmap::07 IO, Network, Data Formats::04 Cryptography

cards.front: What does printf give you over println?
cards.back: C-style format specifiers: %s, %d, %f, %.2f, %n
cards.extra: %n is the platform line separator; a literal \n is not portable. It does not append a newline on its own.
cards.merge_into: 00 Java Roadmap::07 IO, Network, Data Formats::01 I-O Operations

cards.front: How do you run a single Java source file without compiling it first?
cards.back: java Hello.java — the launcher compiles in memory and runs it (Java 11+)
cards.extra: No class file is produced; the file may even declare several classes.
cards.merge_into: 00 Java Roadmap::01 Foundations::02 Basic Syntax

cards.front: How do you query a module at run time?
cards.back: Class.getModule() / ModuleLayer, then getName(), isExported(), canRead()
cards.extra: That is how frameworks decide whether deep reflection is permitted.
cards.merge_into: 00 Java Roadmap::03 Language Features::04 Modules and Linking

cards.front: What are the three built-in class loaders?
cards.back: Bootstrap (core JDK), platform (formerly extension), application (classpath)
cards.extra: Each delegates upward first, which is why a class cannot be shadowed by your own jar.
cards.merge_into: 00 Java Roadmap::13 JVM and Tooling::01 JVM Internals

cards.front: What performance work landed in Java 10?
cards.back: Parallel full GC for G1, application class-data sharing, and thread-local handshakes
cards.extra: The handshakes removed the need for global safepoints on many operations.
cards.merge_into: 00 Java Roadmap::13 JVM and Tooling::01 JVM Internals

cards.front: How does ResourceBundle find the right file?
cards.back: By walking from the most specific locale to the default: Messages_fr_CA → Messages_fr → Messages
cards.extra: Lookup starts at the most specific locale and falls back one step at a time until a bundle is found, ending at the default locale, so translations only need to cover what differs.
cards.merge_into: 00 Java Roadmap::07 IO, Network, Data Formats::13 Internationalization
